title: Simplify model onboarding state machine and shard lifecycle cleanup
creator: Ava Nguyen
description: Refactor the model onboarding pipeline to replace ad-hoc procedural loaders with a small explicit state machine for shard lifecycle, unify manifest parsing to Manifest v2, and separate tokenizer (lexicon) synchronization from weight activation. Goal is to reduce tail latency during model activation, simplify error handling, and make transitions between legacy and v2 formats opt-in via a compatibility shim.
background: Over the past two years the ingest pipeline evolved with multiple format exceptions and special-cased paths to support older checkpoint layouts. This has increased cognitive burden and contributed to intermittent long tail model-load latencies when many small shards are activated concurrently. Tokenizer/lexicon version checks are currently mixed into weight activation and cause redundant I/O on cold starts. Manifest parsing lives in multiple places and depends on older protobuf runtime (v3.8) which we want to upgrade to 3.18 for performance and security fixes.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce a compact state machine that models {PENDING, FETCHING, VERIFYING, PREFETCHED, ACTIVATING, ACTIVE, FAILED} for each shard and is observable via traces
Manifest v2 parser implemented with a single canonical entrypoint and feature-flag driven compatibility shim for legacy manifests
Tokenizer (vocab) sync decoupled from shard activation: lexicon validated and cached before shard ACTIVATING, no duplicate downloads during concurrent activations
End-to-end smoke tests covering legacy and v2 manifests pass in CI
Cold-start 95th-percentile model activation latency reduced by >= 20% in bench harness for typical shard counts (8-64 shards)
No production regressions for 7-day canary (dedicated testing cluster)
tasks: Design state machine API and in-memory lifecycle representation
Implement manifest v2 canonical parser and migration shim
Refactor tokenizer sync into LexiconManager with caching and versioned keys
Replace ad-hoc activation code paths with state transitions and single reconciler loop
Upgrade protobuf runtime to 3.18 and validate manifest parsing performance
Add metrics/tracing for shard states and transition latencies
Create CI smoke tests and a bench harness scenario for cold start activation
Roll out a staged canary and collect telemetry for 7 days
design_notes: The state machine is intentionally small and deterministic; transitions are driven by events (e.g., fetch complete, checksum verified, lexicon ready) rather than implicit try/catch fallthroughs. Manifest v2 is a flatter JSON/protobuf hybrid with explicit 'file_blocks' and checksum fields. The LexiconManager exposes a getOrFetch(vocab_id) that returns a future and ensures a single inflight fetch per vocab id. For backwards compatibility, the shim will translate legacy 'shard_map' layouts into the v2 'file_blocks' schema at parse time.
technical_decisions: 1) Use a single reconciler (actor) per model instance to serialize shard state transitions to avoid thundering herds. 2) Keep lazy activation but introduce a bounded prefetch window controlled by config to limit concurrent fetches. 3) Upgrade protobuf to 3.18 and pin the runtime in the ingest service to avoid surprising transitive upgrades. 4) Use xxhash64 for fast manifest checksum verification (non-cryptographic) and keep SHA256 for end-to-end integrity checks optional behind a config flag.
testing_plan: Unit tests for state transitions and LexiconManager concurrency; integration tests that simulate partial failures (network, missing objects), and CI bench job measuring cold-start activation P50/P95 for small/medium/large shard counts. Create a ded-qa job that runs through legacy manifest translation paths. Canary traffic will run for 7 days with automatic rollback criteria: activation errors spike > 1% or 95th-percentile activation latency increases > 10% relative to baseline.
rollout_plan: Feature-flag the state machine and manifest v2 parsing behind 'ingest.v2' toggle. Deploy to staging, run full integration and bench suite, deploy to a small dedicated cluster for internal canary, then enable on 10% of production model activations for 72h, evaluate telemetry, then ramp to 100% over a week. Keep legacy shim enabled for additional 30 days before removal.
risk_mitigation:
- Keep legacy parser available as fallback at runtime.
- Add detailed traces for each state transition to debug stuck shards.
- Limit parallel fetches via runtime config to avoid saturating object storage.
- Provide a runtime kill-switch to revert to legacy onboarding in case of regression.
